item.content:encoded: The future of Troy Aikman on ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast has become one of the biggest sports media stories of the NFL season. With Aikman’s contract set to expire after Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, speculation about his replacement is heating up. While several names have been mentioned, there is one candidate who makes more sense than anyone else: Peyton Manning. MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 9: All 32 teams ranked worst to first Peyton Manning is the obvious choice to replace Troy Aikman Oct 17, 2019; Denver, CO, USA; FOX Sports broadcaster Troy Aikman before the game between the Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) There has been plenty of discussion about who ESPN could bring in to replace Aikman if he leaves the network. Greg Olsen has emerged as a popular candidate, while Jason Kelce could also be an option given his existing role on the Monday Night Countdown panel. Tony Romo is another name that could generate plenty of attention. The former Cowboys quarterback recently became available after parting ways with CBS. Replacing one Dallas quarterback with another would certainly be an interesting storyline, but Romo is not the answer. Instead, ESPN should make a serious push to bring Manning into the traditional Monday Night Football booth. The Hall of Fame quarterback already has an established relationship with ESPN through the ManningCast, which he hosts alongside his brother, Eli Manning. The alternate broadcast has become a familiar part of ESPN’s Monday Night Football coverage, giving Peyton plenty of experience discussing NFL games in front of a national audience. Manning also brings the credibility, personality, football knowledge, and name recognition that ESPN should want in its lead NFL broadcast booth. Pairing him with Joe Buck would give the network an opportunity to create another high-profile broadcasting partnership. MORE: NFL contenders & pretenders after Week 8 ESPN should make Peyton Manning its top priority Peyton Manning in field before Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts game. Credit: Grace Hollars-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images. There is no shortage of potential candidates, but Manning should be at the top of ESPN’s list. Greg Olsen is a legitimate option, and his past experience as Fox’s lead analyst (before Tom Brady) makes him an attractive candidate. However, Olsen doesn’t bring the same combination of Hall of Fame playing experience, national recognition, and existing ESPN relationship as Manning. The biggest obstacle could be convincing Manning to take on the traditional broadcast role. He has previously declined opportunities to join a regular NFL broadcast booth, and his current arrangement with ESPN allows him to work alongside Eli without the demands of traveling to every game. ESPN would have to make an offer compelling enough to change that. Still, if Aikman is officially finished with Monday Night Football after the Super Bowl, there should be one name at the top of the replacement conversation. Peyton Manning is the logical choice. ESPN should make him its priority, and there really isn’t a close second. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Manchester United fans force Champions League game delay with protest against ownership
item.description: Manchester United fans protested against the team's ownership on Tuesday -Credit:Michael Regan, Getty Images Manchester United fans demonstrated against the club's owners both before and during their match against AS Roma on Tuesday. A group of United supporters began hurling tennis balls and other items onto the Old Trafford pitch. The action commenced at 20 minutes and five seconds, a timeframe chosen to symbolize the year the Glazers took control at Old Trafford. Hero of the night Matheus Cunha was among the players who assisted in clearing the objects from the playing surface. After they were removed, the match was able to continue, as per the Manchester Evening News . Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Goalkeeper involved in tragic Jesús de Miguel collision 'breaks down' after soccer star's death -Credit:Michael Regan, Getty Images Hundreds of yellow and green balloons were also launched from the Stretford End before kickoff as the teams emerged from the tunnel. The demonstration marks the latest in an extended series of protests against United's ownership. Before the Manchester derby on September 13, approximately 500 fans rallied against the club's efforts to eliminate ticket touting. United had anticipated the initiative would end ticket touting, and although the operation was considered successful, they also acknowledged that "some innocent supporters may have been affected". Chants opposing Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers have become a fixture of the United repertoire, with fans directing their frustration at the team's woeful performance toward the owners rather than Michael Carrick. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE However, for the first time since September 10, United fans were given good reason to cheer on their side on Tuesday, coming back from 2-0 down at halftime to beat Roma 3-2. The comeback began courtesy of a Bruno Fernandes penalty, before Cunha equalized with a close-range effort in the 83rd minute thanks in no small part to woeful defending from the visitors. The Brazilian then gave United the lead three minutes later with a thundering effort, prompting him to take off his jersey and dive into the crowd in celebration, leading to a yellow card. This proved costly as the clock wound down, with a rash tackle in the 91st minute leading to a second yellow as the hero of the game was given his marching orders. Regardless, United were able to hold onto the lead and thus end their nine-game winless run.

Starter Jake Matsen broke his collarbone early in the Oct. 8 loss to Corner Canyon, and American Fork’s season went to a senior who had started much of last year and had waited behind Matsen this fall. Childs’ first start came on the road at Skyridge, against the No. 1 seed and the team that ended the Cavemen’s season a year ago. The game started badly. Beckham Bennett scored on two short runs in the first quarter, and Skyridge led 14-0. Then American Fork settled in. The Cavemen outscored the Falcons 15-7 the rest of the way. With 8:21 left, Childs threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Zack Cowie and ran in the two-point conversion himself to make it 21-15. That was as close as they got. Last week Childs looked more comfortable. He threw two touchdown passes in a 32-21 first-round win over Copper Hills, and DC Fonua returned an interception 34 yards for a touchdown and later ran for another. Childs now gets a second chance at Skyridge, with three more weeks of first-team snaps than he had in the first meeting. If American Fork avoids another slow start, this rematch could look different. American Fork has beaten good teams this season. It won 29-21 at Davis, the 6A No. 5 seed, and 28-24 at Lone Peak, the No. 7 seed. It also won road games at 5A quarterfinalist Pleasant Grove (36-16) and at Timpview (28-26). The Cavemen’s October slide began with a 20-19 home loss to Lehi on Oct. 2. Matsen got hurt the next week, and the losses to Corner Canyon and Skyridge followed. The defense is American Fork’s best chance. Noah Behm has six interceptions and two defensive touchdowns, and he’s also the second-leading receiver, with four touchdown catches. Dalin Afu has four sacks and two defensive touchdowns, and Sam Thompson has four sacks. Skyridge quarterback Jagger Fountaine has thrown 11 interceptions, so turnovers are American Fork’s clearest path to an upset. item.title: George Pickens trade update from NFL insider raises eyebrows after Cowboys loss
item.description: George Pickens trade update from NFL insider raises eyebrows after Cowboys loss originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Cowboys fell in yet another close game on Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals , 33-30 in an overtime loss. That puts Dallas at a 3-5 record for the season, which obviously isn't a good look. Heading into their next game against the 2-6 Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, there are a lot of questions about what owner and general manager Jerry Jones may do before the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline. One of the big players that he could possibly move is wide receiver George Pickens. So, will it happen? NFL insider shares latest update on George Pickens trade rumors With all the talk about Pickens possibly getting traded before the trade deadline, one NFL insider is sharing what he's heard. Appearing on the Pat McAfee Show on Tuesday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said , "I was told the Dallas Cowboys aren't trading George Pickens." Zachary Krueger of NBC Sports adds that Rapoport also said, "As of right now, there's nothing there," as far as a potential trade involving the player. "Pickens, who is playing out the season on the franchise tag, hasn't produced at the level he did in 2025 when he broke out for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns, but he remains a focal point in the offense despite his underwhelming production," Krueger adds. "Pickens still ranks 14th in the league among all receivers in targets and is 12th in total air yards. Despite the Cowboys' disappointing 3-5 record, they remain in the race to win what has been an underwhelming NFC East." He adds, "With team owner Jerry Jones saying earlier that Pickens needs to be targeted more, it's safe to assume he will remain with the Cowboys for the season." So, all of that talk and buzz about Pickens getting moved may amount to nothing. But never say never until Nov. 10 has come and gone. item.title: Details emerge following crash that killed 2 Texas Lutheran football players
item.description: Texas Lutheran University will hold a memorial on November 5 for two student-athletes killed in a Seguin crash on State Highway 46. (NurPhoto via Getty Images) Texas Lutheran University is preparing to come together this week to remember two student-athletes killed in a crash in Seguin , as the university's Bulldog community mourns their loss. The university announced a memorial service for A'Jean (AJ) Augustine, 20, of Houston, and Deyreck Dean, 23, of Rockwall, scheduled for 11 a.m. Thursday, November 5, in Jackson Auditorium. "The Bulldog Family is devastated by the loss of two of our own this week," the university said in its announcement. The gathering will give students, faculty, staff, teammates and loved ones an opportunity to celebrate the lives of Augustine and Dean, grieve their absence and pray for their families, according to the university. A short reception will follow the service. Those unable to attend in person can watch the service through a university livestream. Augustine and Dean were killed early Monday, November 2, in a single-vehicle crash on State Highway 46 in Seguin, according to police. The crash was reported at approximately 2:38 a.m. in the 1900 block of State Highway 46 North. A 2012 Kia Sorento was traveling southbound at a high rate of speed when the driver lost control, crossed into the northbound lanes and struck a guardrail, according to a preliminary police report. Both occupants were pronounced dead at the scene. In an earlier statement to MySA, Texas Lutheran described Augustine and Dean as beloved members of the university community whose loss would be felt across campus. Both students were connected to the university's football program. Augustine was an active member of the 2026 team, listed as a junior kicker on the Bulldogs' roster. Dean previously played for the team as a senior linebacker, with his athletic eligibility expiring after the 2025 season. The livestream can be found here. Sign up for Afternoon Headlines, MySA's free newsletter bringing you San Antonio's top stories of the day. This article originally published at Details emerge following crash that killed 2 Texas Lutheran football players .

With Jackson facing another extended absence and his contract approaching a decision point, Wright sees Miami as a destination that could appeal to both the quarterback and a franchise searching for answers. Nick Wright Predicts Lamar Jackson Will Become Dolphins’ Starter Appearing on “The Herd,” Wright made a direct prediction about where Jackson will play next season. “I think Lamar Jackson is the Week 1 starting quarterback next year for the Miami Dolphins,” Wright said in the clip shared by the show . He built his case around Miami potentially holding a valuable draft pick, its financial direction and Jackson’s connection to Florida. “I think the Dolphins are going to have a top-three pick. The Dolphins cleaned up their cap,” Wright said. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “I think he would accept a trade to Miami because of the Florida roots. I think that might be where this is headed.” Miami fell to 1-6 after Sunday’s 24-19 loss to New England. That record makes a high selection plausible, although the final draft order remains months away. Wright’s proposal would give the Dolphins an established quarterback with a résumé few potential acquisitions could match. It would also require Baltimore to entertain moving the player around whom it has built its offense. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator That distinction matters. Jackson’s deal includes a no-trade clause, giving his willingness to approve a destination practical significance. His contract runs through 2027, so a move next offseason would require a transaction while he remains under contract. Jackson’s Latest Injury Raises Difficult Questions for Baltimore The discussion followed Jackson’s thumb injury on Baltimore’s opening offensive snap against Buffalo. He had just returned after missing three games with an ankle injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson would require surgery and go on injured reserve, leaving open the possibility that his season could be over. Baltimore lost 36-10 and dropped to 4-4. Tyler Huntley also exited with a toe injury, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Nick Wright Predicts Lamar Jackson Will Become Dolphins’ Starter Appearing on “The Herd,” Wright made a direct prediction about where Jackson will play next season. “I think Lamar Jackson is the Week 1 starting quarterback next year for the Miami Dolphins,” Wright said in the clip shared by the show . He built his case around Miami potentially holding a valuable draft pick, its financial direction and Jackson’s connection to Florida. “I think the Dolphins are going to have a top-three pick. The Dolphins cleaned up their cap,” Wright said. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “I think he would accept a trade to Miami because of the Florida roots. I think that might be where this is headed.” Miami fell to 1-6 after Sunday’s 24-19 loss to New England. That record makes a high selection plausible, although the final draft order remains months away. Wright’s proposal would give the Dolphins an established quarterback with a résumé few potential acquisitions could match. It would also require Baltimore to entertain moving the player around whom it has built its offense. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator That distinction matters. Wright was predicting a possible outcome, and the supplied clip contained no announcement of trade discussions or a request from Jackson. Jackson’s deal includes a no-trade clause, giving his willingness to approve a destination practical significance. His contract runs through 2027, so a move next offseason would require a transaction while he remains under contract. Jackson’s Latest Injury Raises Difficult Questions for Baltimore The discussion followed Jackson’s thumb injury on Baltimore’s opening offensive snap against Buffalo. He had just returned after missing three games with an ankle injury. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Jackson would require surgery and go on injured reserve, leaving open the possibility that his season could be over. Baltimore lost 36-10 and dropped to 4-4. Tyler Huntley also exited with a toe injury, forcing undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his NFL debut. Those circumstances have sharpened questions about Jackson’s long-term future in Baltimore , with the organization facing decisions about both its immediate quarterback needs and its next contract commitment. “Nobody’s blaming Lamar for the injuries, but what do you do with Lamar? Would you extend him?” Wright asked. “I mean, this is one of the trickiest situations we’ve ever had in the NFL.” Wright emphasized the quality of Jackson’s healthy seasons, citing his first-team All-Pro selections and two league MVP awards. His concern centered on how often Baltimore can count on having that player available. “When he’s out there, he’s as dynamic a regular-season player as we’ve ever seen, but he’s not out there that often,” he said. For Miami, acquiring Jackson would mean weighing that same concern against the opportunity to add an exceptional talent. For Baltimore, any proposal would have to justify surrendering a quarterback capable of defining the franchise. Wright has picked his destination. The Dolphins’ remaining season will help determine whether they possess the draft capital to make that prediction worth a serious phone call. item.title: Yamal And Raphinha Get 8.5 | Barcelona Players Rated In Impressive Win Vs Aston Villa
item.description: Yamal And Raphinha Get 8.5 | Barcelona Players Rated In Impressive Win Vs Aston Villa Barcelona entertained Aston Villa at the Nou Camp earlier tonight as they hoped to secure a win at home in the UEFA Champions League. The Catalan giants made a quick start to the game and got their noses ahead in the seventh minute thanks to Lamine Yamal’s goal. Hansi Flick’s men went into the half-time break 1-0 up on the scoreline. Raphinha doubled Barca’s advantage in the 52nd minute before going on to score again in the 64th minute. The match ended with the Catalan giants securing an impressive 3-0 win at the Nou Camp. Let’s take a look at how each Barcelona player fared during the clash against the Villans. GK: Joan Garcia – 7/10 Garcia made one solid save at the back and did well to secure a clean sheet tonight. RB: Brian Farinas – 7/10 He came back to defend when needed and was tidy with his ball distribution. CB: Pau Cubarsi – 7/10 Cubarsi gave a good account of himself on the defensive end of the field and was a strong presence in the air. CB: Gerard Martin – 7.5/10 He cleared his lines when he could and was good on the ball. BARCELONA, SPAIN – NOVEMBER 03: Raphinha of FC Barcelona celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammate Lamine Yamal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa FC at Camp Nou on November 03, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) LB: Joao Cancelo – 8/10 He was a positive influence at both ends of the field and has an assist to show for his efforts. CM: Pedri – 7/10 Pedri anchored the midfield well and made two good chances going forward. CM: Rodri – 6.5/10 He anchored the midfield relatively well but offered very little in the final third. CM: Fermin Lopez – 8/10 Lopez was a constant menace inside the opponent’s half and has an assist to his name. RW: Lamine Yamal – 8.5/10 He made a few dangerous runs with the ball and managed to score the opener in the seventh minute ST: Raphinha – 8.5/10 Raphinha scored a quick-fire brace in the second half to help Barcelona secure a convincing win tonight. LW: Anthony Gordon – 7.5/10 He caught the eye at times, but there was no goal for him. CM: Marc Bernal – 6.5/10 He offered decent protection for his teammates at the back. ST: Gabriel Jesus – 7/10 Jesus was lively after coming off the bench. CM: Frenkie de Jong – 6/10 He offered very little after coming on in the 69th minute. Gavi made one good chance in the final third.

item.title: NASCAR VP explains Carson Hocevar, Josh Berry penalties
item.description: Motorsport photo NASCAR Vice President of Competition Elton Sawyer took to SiriusXM Radio on Tuesday to explain the rationale behind a pair of penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for brake checking over the weekend at Martinsville Speedway. First and foremost, the decision to issue the $100,000 fine to Hocevar and the $50,000 fine to Berry, plus 25 driver points each, came down to SMT data. NASCAR could see very decisively that both drivers retaliated on Sunday by slamming on their brakes and literally destroying the cars behind them. In the case of Hocevar, the Spire No. 77 hard braked directly in front of Austin Cindric four times on the straightaways, even with spotter Tyler Green saying repeatedly ‘Carson stop,’ without a commensurate response. Spire Motorsports took independent action from NASCAR earlier in the day by suspending Hocevar for the season finale this weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Berry hard braked once on corner exit ahead of Ryan Blaney , which also forced the victim to go behind the wall, and Sawyer told Sirius Speedway host Dave Moody that this would not be tolerated. Read Also: NASCAR issues penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for Martinsville brake-checks Spire Motorsports suspends Carson Hocevar, parking him for NASCAR finale “I think the world that we live in today with the amount of data we can pull off the cars and go back and review that, we can make better decisions,” Sawyer said. “The one thing that I would add and something that we're looking at is how we can do a better job, we as NASCAR, do a better job in officiating this within the race. “We would love to not be talking about this today, would love to be talking about going to Homestead-Miami to crown three very deserving champions, whoever they may be, Friday night, Saturday or Sunday, but unfortunately, we're talking about this today. But what we really strive is to get it right. And sometimes you have to wait just a little bit to get all the data and get all the information to be able to do that.” With that said, Sawyer does aim for NASCAR to move towards being more capable of making just calls in real time. Sawyer explained that NASCAR took this very seriously because it was the drivers that came to the Sanctioning Body and asked for softer bumpers in the first place. Some wanted softer bumpers to lessen the impact felt by drivers in the cars. Others wanted softer front bumpers to prevent drivers from divebombing each other in lieu of cleaner passes. So that Hocevar and Berry weaponized that on Sunday required a response. “We knew Martinsville would be the first test as far as being able to, how they could bump and run, and that's part of our DNA, that's part of Martinsville,” Sawyer said. “But what rose to a level of real concern for us was that they had taken the structure of the front of the car and used that as an antic or a strategy to basically ruin other drivers' days and then we felt like we had to step in.” Hocevar was fined $10
item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo NASCAR Vice President of Competition Elton Sawyer took to SiriusXM Radio on Tuesday to explain the rationale behind a pair of penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for brake checking over the weekend at Martinsville Speedway. First and foremost, the decision to issue the $100,000 fine to Hocevar and the $50,000 fine to Berry, plus 25 driver points each, came down to SMT data. NASCAR could see very decisively that both drivers retaliated on Sunday by slamming on their brakes and literally destroying the cars behind them. In the case of Hocevar, the Spire No. 77 hard braked directly in front of Austin Cindric four times on the straightaways, even with spotter Tyler Green saying repeatedly ‘Carson stop,’ without a commensurate response. Spire Motorsports took independent action from NASCAR earlier in the day by suspending Hocevar for the season finale this weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Berry hard braked once on corner exit ahead of Ryan Blaney , which also forced the victim to go behind the wall, and Sawyer told Sirius Speedway host Dave Moody that this would not be tolerated. Read Also: NASCAR issues penalties to Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry for Martinsville brake-checks Spire Motorsports suspends Carson Hocevar, parking him for NASCAR finale “I think the world that we live in today with the amount of data we can pull off the cars and go back and review that, we can make better decisions,” Sawyer said. “The one thing that I would add and something that we're looking at is how we can do a better job, we as NASCAR, do a better job in officiating this within the race. “We would love to not be talking about this today, would love to be talking about going to Homestead-Miami to crown three very deserving champions, whoever they may be, Friday night, Saturday or Sunday, but unfortunately, we're talking about this today. But what we really strive is to get it right. And sometimes you have to wait just a little bit to get all the data and get all the information to be able to do that.” With that said, Sawyer does aim for NASCAR to move towards being more capable of making just calls in real time. Sawyer explained that NASCAR took this very seriously because it was the drivers that came to the Sanctioning Body and asked for softer bumpers in the first place. Some wanted softer bumpers to lessen the impact felt by drivers in the cars. Others wanted softer front bumpers to prevent drivers from divebombing each other in lieu of cleaner passes. So that Hocevar and Berry weaponized that on Sunday required a response. “We knew Martinsville would be the first test as far as being able to, how they could bump and run, and that's part of our DNA, that's part of Martinsville,” Sawyer said. “But what rose to a level of real concern for us was that they had taken the structure of the front of the car and used that as an antic or a strategy to basically ruin other drivers' days and then we felt like we had to step in.” Hocevar was fined $100,000 compared to the $50,000 for Berry because Sawyer said NASCAR has had numerous 'behavioral meetings' with the young driver over the past several years. "We just felt like after reviewing all the data and the audio, that this one rose to a level that it needed to be more than just the 50,000 that Josh got," Sawyer said. Sawyer also said that Spire's decision to suspend Hocevar had no bearing on what NASCAR chose to do. That was an entirely independent choice. The obvious question after all of this is if NASCAR went too far in softening the front bumpers and if the league needs to reverse course. Sawyer said no, but hedged the answer with a maybe at the same time. “We know a lot more today than we knew yesterday, and we'll know a lot more tomorrow about this situation as far as the car and how we want to react going forward with it,” Sawyer said. “But we're always learning, as we've said many, many times. And this is a safety initiative that our sport has had for decades and it's not a destination, it's a journey. “We'll continue to look at the cars and what we can do to make them as safe as possible. We know that motorsports in general is inherently a dangerous sport and we want to do everything we can to make our competitors and our fans as safe as possible. “So to get to the actual point there, we will go back and look at this and see what adjustments we can make to the car that will also give us some of the best racing, short track racing that our fans deserve and that is a little bumping and moving cars and the tire marks – things we have accustomed to loving about our short tracks. So yes, we will address that as well.” To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: The polls are open! Vote for the top Tulare County athlete of the week
item.description: Visalia Times-Delta/Tulare Advance-Register readers can now vote for their favorite high school athletes. The poll closes at noon Friday, Nov. 6. There are no restrictions, so vote now and vote often. Please do not email your votes. Here are the choices for this week: Adan Aldana, football, Woodlake: Aldana rumbled for 122 yards rushing and a touchdown to lift the Tigers to an outright East Sequoia League championship. Connor Cain, football, Golden West: Cain scored 4 total touchdowns (3 receiving, 1 rushing) and finished with 8 catches for 89 yards as the Trailblazers won their fourth straight Battle for the Saddle rivalry game. Leonardo Coronado, football, Orosi: Coronado rushed for 128 yards and 3 touchdowns as the Cardinals captured an outright East Sequoia League-Redwood championship. Emma Crisp, girls flag football, Redwood: Crisp passed for 326 yards and 4 touchdowns in a shutout playoff win over Lompoc. Mike Ennis, football, Porterville: Ennis was nearly perfect in the Granite Bowl victory, completing 18-of-20 passes for 231 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also ran for 101 yards and scored 3 rushing touchdowns. J.J. Guereca, football, Lindsay: Guereca caught 3 passes for 125 yards and 2 touchdowns as the Cardinals won the Bell Game. Nash McElree, football, Redwood: McElree completed 82% of his throws, hitting 19-of-23 passes for 251 yards and 2 touchdowns to lead the Rangers to a win in the annual Cowhide rivalry game. Landan Seechan, football, Tulare Western: Seechan scored a receiving touchdown to help the Mustangs win the Bell Game for the first time since 2019. VOTE HERE More: Tulare Western clinches outright EYL title with Bell Game win More: See the first-round matchups for Tulare County football teams How to nominate an Athlete of the Week Nominations are based on information available to the Times-Delta. All high school varsity players from Tulare County can be on the ballot. Nominations must be received by Monday morning following that week's games for consideration. Anyone can nominate an athlete of the week for every sport. Nominate next week’s ballot through email. Readers can email nominations to sports reporter Vongni Yang at vyang2@visaliatimesdelta.com. Please include a player’s statistics and a photo if possible. This article originally appeared on Visalia Times-Delta: The polls are open! Vote for the top Tulare County athlete of the week

item.title: ‘A lot of lies’ – Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was ‘right’ to drop him against Bournemouth and denies rift
item.description: ‘A lot of lies’ – Bruno Fernandes says Michael Carrick was ‘right’ to drop him against Bournemouth and denies rift Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes insists there are no issues between him and boss Michael Carrick – and hopes his side’s win over Roma can be the start of a turnaround this season. The 3-2 victory provided a much-needed boost for United following a run of nine games without a win. Fernandes was dropped to the bench for his side’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth last month following comments made after their 4-1 loss to Como, in which he questioned the team’s approach . But the United skipper played down any perceived problems between him and Carrick and says he is firmly focused on turning things around. “The club needed that win, the players needed that win,” he told Amazon Prime. “We have been working so hard to get out of this situation all together. “It’s been tough, there’s been a lot of speculation in the media. A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, that we have cleared the air after. Nothing like that happened. “The manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I wasn’t performing and that’s fair. “Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. If it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions. I have to accept that. “It doesn’t change the belief I have in the manager and the staff and every player in this club. It doesn’t change my aim to win every game that I have ahead of me.” United have faced mounting pressure following their recent struggles, with supporters growing increasingly frustrated by the team’s performances. Fernandes acknowledged those frustrations but stressed that the players were equally desperate to turn their fortunes around. “It’s been a long time that we didn’t get the win and it’s been frustrating for them as much as it has been for us too,” he said. “But we didn’t take that in the wrong way. We took it in a good way because it’s normal, because fans want to win games. “They’ve been used to seeing this club at the top winning games and winning trophies and for them it’s been so frustrating to see the club in this situation. “I want to make everyone aware that we are all frustrated with the situation at the moment and we all want to get out of this. Hopefully this win today is the start of something good for us.” Reflecting on the comeback victory over Roma, in which United came from two goals down thanks to a Fernandes penalty and Matheus Cunha double, the Portugal international urged his side to build on the win. “It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to perform in the way we want, to get the results we want,” he added. “We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a full game to get more results and it’s been tough. “But today was important to get a win. We knew after half-time we still had the fans with us, we felt at any moment that we could change

item.title: USA Soccer’s Balogun Returns To Action For Monaco
item.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Training - University of Washington, Seattle, Washington, U.S. - July 3, 2026 Folarin Balogun of the U.S. during training IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Steven Bisig Folarin Balogun finally broke his scoring drought for Monaco. The United States men’s national team striker is back in the mix for the Conference League, according to Fox Sports . He earned his spot after Ansu Fati got hurt and had to leave the squad list. This move clears a huge path for Balogun to get more playing time. It also fixes a strange situation that kept him on the bench for weeks. The change happened right before the next round of games. Balogun’s name now appears on the official roster shown on Tuesday. He was missing from the list just a short time ago. The club decided to swap him in because Fati cannot play. The French daily L’Equipe reported that Fati is out for two months. He suffered the injury in a match against Lille on Oct. 25. That gap left Monaco needing a forward, and Balogun stepped up. A Rough Path to the Field Getting to this point was not easy for the American striker. He only played as a substitute this season. He has featured in five games total. A 3-1 defeat at Paris FC on Sunday marked his first goal of the season. That goal matters more now because it ends a dry spell. It also proves he can score even when the team struggles. The road to this moment was blocked by transfer drama. Balogun was close to joining Everton in late August. A deal for a reported £40 million (with add-ons) was on the table. He pulled out of the move at the last minute . Doubts from the English club regarding his health made him uneasy. He did not want to sign with a team that questioned his medical results. This decision kept him at Monaco, but it caused confusion. World Cup Drama and New Chances The striker faced other hurdles before this season even started. A red card during the World Cup caused a major controversy. He got the card in a win over Bosnia and Herzegovina. The suspension was one game, but it was deferred by FIFA. U.S. President Donald Trump intervened to help. Gianni Infantino received a call to check if the red card review was possible. The request worked. Balogun was allowed to play in the round of 16. He had a forgettable performance as the U.S. lost to Belgium. Now the focus shifts to the upcoming matches. The Conference League saw Monaco secure victories in its opening two matches. They beat CSKA Sofia and Freiburg. The team has tough matches coming up. They will play FC Nordsjælland on Thursday. They also face Hearts, Brighton, and Lincoln Red Imps later. Balogun needs to keep scoring if he wants to stay in the starting lineup. The clock is ticking for him to prove he is ready. The squad list is set, and he is now one of the forwards. Fans will watch closely to see if he can lead the attack.

item.title: Man Utd snap winless streak with Roma comeback
item.description: Matheus Cunha scored twice in Manchester United's comeback against Roma (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United roared back from 2-0 down to give beleaguered manager Michael Carrick a lifeline with a memorable 3-2 win over Roma at Old Trafford. The unrest among the home fans bordered on mutiny after Roma surged into a 2-0 lead inside 20 minutes through Matias Soule and Donyell Malen. But United ended a nine-game winless run in all competitions thanks to Matheus Cunha's double after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had reduced the deficit. "This place does incredible things, does magical things," said Carrick. "I spoke with them at half-time a little bit about how this place can change and it only takes one moment. It certainly did that and the boys made every little bit of every little opportunity. Fantastic in the end." The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of four previous defeats at Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini's men lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. "A game lasts 90 minutes," said Gasperini. "They stepped it up in the second half but we could have done more to safeguard the score." - Cunha's costly celebration - Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez's foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora's pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Malen converted a penalty after Soule's shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United's unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick's luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. But United ended a nine-game winless run in all competitions thanks to Matheus Cunha's double after a twice-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty had reduced the deficit. "This place does incredible things, does magical things," said Carrick. "I spoke with them at half-time a little bit about how this place can change and it only takes one moment. It certainly did that and the boys made every little bit of every little opportunity. Fantastic in the end." The decision to hand Carrick a stay of execution looked to have backfired in a lifeless first half United performance. Roma, though, failed to slay their ghosts of four previous defeats at Old Trafford in another spectacular Champions League collapse. Gian Piero Gasperini's men lost 4-3 to Real Madrid last month after leading 3-1 with just eight minutes remaining. "A game lasts 90 minutes," said Gasperini. "They stepped it up in the second half but we could have done more to safeguard the score." - Cunha's costly celebration - Carrick reacted to Lisandro Martinez's foolish red card in a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday by dropping the Argentine international. It made little difference as his disorganised defence was torn apart inside the opening 20 minutes. Soule was afforded acres of space to control Rodrigo Mora's pass and slot past Senne Lammens on 11 minutes. Moments later United were left completely exposed again down their left and Malen converted a penalty after Soule's shot hit the outstretched hand of Ayden Heaven. The game was temporarily stopped midway through the first half by supporters throwing tennis balls onto the field, accompanied by chants calling for with United's unpopular owners, the American-based Glazer family, to sell the club. United were dealt a further blow inside two minutes of the second half when £70 million ($94 million) signing Carlos Baleba pulled up with a suspected severe hamstring injury after bursting into the Roma box. Yet, Carrick's luck turned just before the hour mark when Cunha won a generous penalty award for minimal contact by Gianluca Mancini. Fernandes's first spot-kick was saved by Roma's third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vasquez, but was given a reprieve by encroaching by the visitors. The United captain smashed home at the second attempt to kickstart the comeback. Seconds later Bryan Mbeumo hit the inside of both posts after being played in by Cunha. United were gifted the equaliser seven minutes from time when Leonardo Balerdi's swipe at fresh air gave Cunha the simplest task to tap in. Three minutes later, the Brazilian thundered a shot past Vasquez at his near post and flung himself into the crowd in what proved to be a costly celebration. Cunha was booked and then shown a second yellow card moments later for a wild lunge in stoppage time. But the 10 men held on to breathe new life into United's Champions League campaign after back-to-back defeats against Atletico Madrid and Como. Whether it proves to be a turning point or just another temporary reprieve for Carrick remains to be seen. "It's one game, so it depends on what happens next and we've got to capitalise on that," added Carrick. "To see the supporters going home happy, it's what we live for. To give them performances and nights like this." kca/lp

item.title: Colton Herta to run Cadillac FP1 in Brazil as FIA superlicense quest continues
item.description: Motorsport photo Cadillac test driver Colton Herta will conduct his sixth Friday practice session of the F1 season at this weekend's Sao Paulo GP to collect his missing FIA superlicense point required to race in the series. Herta, who has been building up for an F1 campaign with private testing, FP1 sessions and a troubled F2 campaign, needs 40 points to obtain the required FIA superlicense. Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results. Cadillac will now rectify that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car, which yields a single point. Teams are only required to run a rookie in four FP1 sessions per year, but Sao Paulo will be Herta's sixth of the season as the squad is keen for Herta to finally obtain the license. That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Valtteri Bottas for a second year alongside Perez, or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027. "I’m really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the MAC-26 for another FP1 session," Herta said. "Interlagos is such an iconic, historic track, and driving an F1 car around there is going to be an awesome experience. "Every time I’ve stepped into the car this year, from Barcelona to Budapest, COTA and Mexico City, I’ve felt more comfortable and better integrated with the engineering team. My goal for Friday morning in Brazil is the same: execute the run plan cleanly, give Checo and the engineers the best possible setup data to start their weekend, and keep building on my progress in the car. I’m grateful to the team for giving me this opportunity." Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing crash Cadillac heads to Brazil after a bruising Mexico weekend, which ended with Bottas suffering a high-speed crash in the race due to a sudden front-left suspension failure. Team principal Marcin Budkowski said the team had "implemented mitigations" to avoid a repeat. "Following our post-race investigations, Valtteri suffered a suspension failure, and we have implemented mitigations going forward," Budkowski said. "I’m also pleased to see Colton return to the MAC-26 for another FP1 outing, stepping in for Checo. His growth in the car across his sessions has been impressive, and his feedback remains invaluable to our 2027 development program." Herta's bid to obtain his superlicense hit a snag when his car broke down in Monza, leaving the 26-year-old short of the 100km threshold required for the session to award a point. In Brazil, 24 laps of the Interlagos circuit will satisfy that requirement. item.title: Warriors Proposed To Trade Kristaps Porzingis For NBA’s Best Rebounder
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 25: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors looks on during a break in play against the Brooklyn Nets during the first half at Chase Center on March 25, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Kelley L Cox/Getty Images) Getty Domantas Sabonis wants to leave Kings Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors lack frontcourt depth, and the absence of Kristaps Porzingis to begin the year has been a big hit for the team hoping to stay competitive in the final seasons left in the Stephen Curry era. The Warriors are reportedly exploring a Porzingis trade, and with that, a few replacement options have emerged as names the team could go after to capitalize on the time left they have with Curry. With that, one big man in particular who remains a top Warriors trade target is Domantas Sabonis of the Sacramento Kings, and in a new proposal, Golden State takes a big risk to add the center, who is not happy playing for his current team, to land a solid Porzingis replacement. Warriors Domantas Sabonis Trade Idea Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 21: Domantas Sabonis #11 of the Sacramento Kings looks on against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome on October 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Writing for Bleacher Report amid Golden State’s need to upgrade the frontcourt and add a Porzingis replacement, Andy Bailey offered up a Warriors trade proposal that sees the team add Sabonis from the Kings. Here’s his trade idea: Golden State Warriors Receive: Domantas Sabonis Sacramento Kings Receive: Draymond Green (trade-eligible on December 15), Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard and a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick “The Golden State Warriors’ better-than-expected start makes a Draymond Green trade harder to imagine, but they look like a near-ideal landing spot for Sabonis, and they simply can’t get him without including Green or Jimmy Butler,” he wrote. “The more logical approach, assuming the Warriors really want to chase one more title with Stephen Curry, is to pair Green’s salary with the Kristaps Porziņģis contract, which was essentially designed to be a human trade exception.” Moving Green might be difficult for the Warriors, but as seen with his recent ejection , there’s clearly still some major holes i
item.content:encoded: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 25: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors looks on during a break in play against the Brooklyn Nets during the first half at Chase Center on March 25, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Kelley L Cox/Getty Images) Getty Domantas Sabonis wants to leave Kings Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors lack frontcourt depth, and the absence of Kristaps Porzingis to begin the year has been a big hit for the team hoping to stay competitive in the final seasons left in the Stephen Curry era. The Warriors are reportedly exploring a Porzingis trade, and with that, a few replacement options have emerged as names the team could go after to capitalize on the time left they have with Curry. With that, one big man in particular who remains a top Warriors trade target is Domantas Sabonis of the Sacramento Kings, and in a new proposal, Golden State takes a big risk to add the center, who is not happy playing for his current team, to land a solid Porzingis replacement. Warriors Domantas Sabonis Trade Idea Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 21: Domantas Sabonis #11 of the Sacramento Kings looks on against the Los Angeles Clippers at Intuit Dome on October 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) Writing for Bleacher Report amid Golden State’s need to upgrade the frontcourt and add a Porzingis replacement, Andy Bailey offered up a Warriors trade proposal that sees the team add Sabonis from the Kings. Here’s his trade idea: Golden State Warriors Receive: Domantas Sabonis Sacramento Kings Receive: Draymond Green (trade-eligible on December 15), Kristaps Porziņģis, Will Richard and a top-four protected 2032 first-round pick “The Golden State Warriors’ better-than-expected start makes a Draymond Green trade harder to imagine, but they look like a near-ideal landing spot for Sabonis, and they simply can’t get him without including Green or Jimmy Butler,” he wrote. “The more logical approach, assuming the Warriors really want to chase one more title with Stephen Curry, is to pair Green’s salary with the Kristaps Porziņģis contract, which was essentially designed to be a human trade exception.” Moving Green might be difficult for the Warriors, but as seen with his recent ejection , there’s clearly still some major holes in his game, as he isn’t the same type of player he was during the team’s dynasty run a decade ago. Sabonis is also reportedly frustrated in Sacramento right now, and if he is available in a trade for a team like Golden State, he could be a huge upgrade, especially with Porzingis still out. Domantas Sabonis is unhappy and wants out of Sacramento, per @BannedMacMahon “Quite frankly, Sabonis wants out of there, and if they can move him, they would. So he's not happy.” pic.twitter.com/YqLwiU5jAf — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 2, 2026 “Sabonis would be a dramatic upgrade over Green in scoring and rebounding. He’s at least as good a passer (though maybe not quite as good a creator). And it’s easy to imagine the fit between him and Yaxel Lendeborg. Curry’s off-ball movement around either (or both) of those interior hubs would be nearly impossible to stop,” Bailey added. “It’s maybe a harder sell on the other side of the deal. Neither vet seems like a longterm option for Sacramento, but Green’s deal is expiring and Porziņģis’ is only guaranteed for $3 million. They represent an opportunity for flexibility, while Sabonis’ deal is guaranteed for $48.6 million next season.” A Warriors trade proposal like this one, though risky, could be the franchise’s best option to move on from Porzingis while staying competitive after going on a hot streak to begin the 2026-27 season. Why Golden State Lands A Kristaps Porzingis Replacement Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA – MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) As mentioned, the Warriors are reportedly exploring the possibility of trading Porzingis, as he remains out indefinitely with the POTS illness he picked up a few years ago, and has yet to spend pretty much any time with the team. “Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN,” Shams Charania wrote in a post on X. Golden State has started exploring trade routes for Kristaps Porzingis, who is now seriously contemplating his future in basketball as he deals with recurring symptoms from the autoimmune condition termed as POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome), sources tell ESPN. pic.twitter.com/w9fb2Tk4kb — Shams Charania (@ShamsCharania) October 21, 2026 “Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December,” ESPN’s Anthony Slater wrote in subsequent reporting. With that, Sabonis becomes a very realistic replacement option. He isn’t the same caliber player he was a few seasons ago, but remains an offensive hub who could help the Warriors stay competitive over the next few seasons. The center’s scoring numbers are down, but he is averaging a league-leading 14.6 rebounds , along with 6.9 assists, while shooting 71.2% so far this year. His trade value might be low right now, and though the Warriors would have to give up Green in a trade to match salaries, this could be the one final risk Golden State takes to give Curry another shot at leading the team to a fifth title. Just a trade idea, but perhaps one the Warriors should entertain, as Porzingis remains out, and there’s no timeline for when or if he’ll ever play in the Bay Area again. item.title: Funke Akindele, Waje & Shoday’s London Looks Belong in Our Style Notes | See Photos
item.description: Funke Akindele, Shoday, and Waje smiling during their London promotional walk ahead of The Four UK premiere. Upon seeing these photos of Funke Akindele , Shoday and Waje , we had no choice but to pull out our notes, ready for some styling lessons. Did you see how they coordinated their looks for their London outing? Funke and Waje gave us matching buba and iro sets with colourful floral details, while Shoday arrived with a custom embroidered blazer that made its own case for a place in our style notes. The trio were in the UK for the promotional campaign of The Four: No One Fights Alone , and the outing came with another exciting update. Funke Akindele Network and FilmOne Entertainment have announced that the film will have its UK premiere on 29 November at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square in London, ahead of its worldwide cinema release on 11 December. Now, if you’re wondering how Funke and Waje managed to wear matching outfits without looking identical, the answer is in the details. Both looks started with off-white textured cotton, but the floral appliqués gave each one a distinct finish. Funke’s outfit features crimson-red roses with spiral stitching across the bodice and bell sleeves, while yellow sunflowers and leafy green stems run down her wrapper. She completed the look with a golden-yellow head wrap, layered gold necklaces, a broad cuff bracelet and metallic red platform sandals. Funke Akindele Buba and Iro Outfit for The Four London Promo Waje went for lavender roses across the neckline and sleeves of her blouse, with large green floral appliqués decorating the hem of her wrapper. She kept the colour story going with a matching lavender-trimmed scarf, a gold necklace accented with turquoise stones, coordinating earrings and multi-coloured platform heels. Same base colour, different floral story. We love that. Waje outdoors in London promoting The Four: No One Fights Alone in a lavender floral buba and iro set. And Shoday? He clearly had no plans to be the odd one out. His single-breasted blazer featured bold chevron embroidery in turquoise, yellow, red and blue, worn over a beige mesh-knit top and cream wide-leg trousers. Stacked silver Cuban-link chains and dark dress shoes completed the look, giving the colourful jacket room to do its thing. Shoday in a custom geometric chevron-embroidered blazer during The Four promotional tour in London. With the fashion notes taken, we’re also looking forward to seeing what the cast has in store for the London premiere. The Four: No One Fights Alone features Funke Akindele, Waje, Chioma Akpotha, Bisola Aiyeola, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Lateef Adedimeji, Timini Egbuson and Uzor Arukwe, among others. The film premieres at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square on 29 November before its global cinema release on 11 December. Funke Akindele, Waje, and Shoday stepping out in London in coordinated buba and iro and custom tailoring ahead of The Four UK premiere at ODEON Luxe Leicester Square. Waje, Shoday, and Funke Akindele

item.title: The Wendy’s JRPG Is a Searing Anti-Capitalist Screed About Humans Making Real Art
item.description: Over the past year, Wendy’s — yes, the same Wendy’s known for its square burgers, thick milkshakes, and unlikely stewardship of a mid-tier donut chain — has made waves through a series of unconventional creative partnerships. Amid slumps in sales and attention , Wendy’s has turned to popular artistic mediums, like music and video games, to try and reverse course.

item.title: Canva is announcing changes and layoffs affecting 22 percent of its staff
item.description: Canva is making significant changes affecting 1,271 people, which is 22 percent of its staff, co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins announced today . "For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs," says Perkins. "Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today." In her note to staff, Perkins says that: After exploring a wide range of alternatives, I've come to the difficult conclusion that small changes won't be enough. To set ourselves up for the next decade, we need to refound Canva, getting back to our roots of small, … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Obi exhausted from campaign schedule, but in good health — NDC
item.description: The Deputy Spokesperson of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Sam Omale, has said the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, is in good health, attributing concerns about his condition to exhaustion from a demanding campaign schedule. Omale said Obi had been advised to take some rest following hectic engagements involving frequent travels between cities and attendance at multiple political activities. He spoke on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Tuesday while responding to concerns about Obi’s health, particularly after his recent campaign rally in Enugu State, where he reportedly indicated plans to take a break. The campaign council’s deputy spokesperson described Obi as being in good health, insisting that the exhaustion would not affect his campaign activities. “If you know the person of Mr Peter Obi, he is so passionate for this country and he is pouring out his life. Sometimes, I wonder where he gets his energy from,” Omale said. “Today, he is in London this night; the following morning, he is in Enugu. The exhaustion comes in. A human being is a human being. “But he is in perfect health; nothing is wrong with him. It is just exhaustion, and we are trying to calm him down to take a sleep.” He said Obi often combined several activities at the same time, including attending engagements, answering questions and responding to emails. According to him, the former Anambra State governor would continue with town hall meetings before the commencement of the main campaign rallies. “So, it is pure exhaustion, which definitely has no impact on the campaign we are conducting. He is going to continue the town halls before the main rallies begin. He is fine,” Omale added. However, the NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said he was unaware that the party’s presidential candidate had experienced exhaustion arising from campaign activities. Director, who said he had spent time with Obi in Bayelsa State, maintained that he had no knowledge of any health-related incident involving the presidential candidate. “I knew nothing happened to Peter Obi. Honestly, I am not being sarcastic here. As far as I am concerned and as far as I know, Peter Obi is with his health,” he said. He added that he was with Obi in Bayelsa for a day and learnt that the presidential candidate had travelled abroad, noting that some people had accompanied him to the airport. “So, I don’t know where the story of exhaustion came from. So, Omale is in a better position to elucidate the point he has made,” he said. Director further said the national campaign council had not taken any steps to ask Obi to slow down his activities, adding that he was unaware of any development that would require such intervention. The post Obi exhausted from campaign schedule, but in good health — NDC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister
item.description: The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution. Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu. He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications. “I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said. Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…” When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.” He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity. “Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said. The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy. “Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said. However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements. “Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added. Tinubu’s academic qualifications have continued to attract public scrutiny, particularly following the controversy surrounding his Chicago State University records during the 2023 presidential election petition. The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections. The post Tinubu graduated with first-class in accounting — Education minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Akume’s allies disown Alia’s campaign council as Benue APC supremacy war deepens
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A fresh supremacy battle has erupted in the Benue State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, following the rejection of about 500-man campaign council for President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia by the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, a political mobilisation platform associated with the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume. The disagreement followed Monday’s announcement by the APC State Organising Secretary, James Ornguga, of a joint campaign council for Tinubu and Alia ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also fixed Thursday, November 5, for the inauguration of the council in Makurdi, with a supplementary list expected to be released later. However, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027, in a disclaimer issued Tuesday and signed by its Director-General, Chief Akange Audu, disowned the purported campaign structure, alleging that the names of its conveners, members and political candidates had been included without their authorisation. The Alliance specifically faulted the inclusion of its conveners, Senator Jack Tilley-Gyado, and Elder Simon Shango, as well as its candidates for the National Assembly and Benue State House of Assembly, in the list of the purported Alia campaign council. It stated, “for the avoidance of doubt, the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 categorically dissociates itself from the said publication and disowns any claim or suggestion that the individuals mentioned therein are associated with, or constitute members of, the purported Alia Campaign structure.” The group further questioned the political arrangement that reportedly placed Governor Alia as chairman of the campaign council while listing Akume, whom it described as the founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, as merely a member. According to the Alliance, “We find it particularly contentious that a purported Alia Campaign structure would designate Governor Hyacinth Alia as its Chairman while listing the Founder and foremost political leader of the APC in Benue State, Sen. George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.” The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. This has contributed to the divisions and disagreements currently affecting the party in the state.” Despite rejecting the campaign council, the group insisted that “the Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu 2027 remains committed to its stated mandate of mobilising support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. “Our political engagement also extends to supporting APC candidates for the National Assembly and the Benue State House of Assembly who emerge from the list and leadership direction recognised by our leader, Sen. George Akume.” The Alliance al

George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, merely as a member.” The Akume-aligned group alleged that “since the APC secured victory in the 2023 general elections, the party’s established leadership and structures have, in practical terms, been sidelined by the Alia administration. item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

item.title: Ubisoft Makes Bid to Purchase Xbox Studio on the Brink of Closure
item.description: Microsoft intends to divest from Dishonored and Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Studios as part of its mass layoffs at Xbox and other Microsoft divisions. item.title: Rising feed costs threaten poultry, livestock farming in 3 states
item.description: Farmers in Niger, Kogi and Nasarawa states have warned that rising feed costs, expensive day-old chicks and poor market prices threaten livestock production and livelihoods. They said the situation had forced some operators to reduce production, sell their animals at losses or abandon farming altogether. The farmers spoke in separate interviews with the News Agency of Nigeria on Tuesday during a nationwide survey in Minna. They identified high feed costs, which account for 70 to 80 per cent of poultry production expenses, as their biggest challenge. They called for subsidised feed ingredients, affordable financing, improved access to essential inputs and local feed mills to reduce production costs. In Kogi, a poultry farmer and retired Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security director, Mr Dare Olukaiyeja, said feeding accounted for 80 per cent of his production costs. Olukaiyeja, who keeps 250 birds, said a crate of eggs currently sold for about N6,200 amid declining consumer purchasing power. Similarly, Mr Shola Adeyi, a Lokoja-based farmer with a 1,000-bird capacity, said feed prices had increased by N2,000 to N3,000 per bag almost monthly since January. He said starter, finisher and layer feeds sold for N22,500, N22,000 and N16,000 respectively, while day-old chicks cost about N2,200 each. Adeyi identified unreliable electricity, extreme heat and high bird mortality as additional challenges confronting poultry farmers. He said some operators had abandoned the business because they could not afford alternative power sources. He said eggs sold for between N6,000 and N6,500 per crate, while broilers fetched N4,500 to N5,000 per kilogramme. According to him, the prices barely covered production costs, necessitating long-term subsidised or interest-free loans and effective market regulation. Another farmer, Mr Malik Ajayi, said day-old chick and feed prices usually increased during Sallah, Easter and Christmas. Ajayi, who rears broilers, cockerels and foreign turkeys, said he recently bought three cartons of day-old chicks for N352,500. He attributed some price fluctuations to possible exploitation by large-scale producers and urged the government to introduce effective price regulation. Ajayi, who keeps 150 broilers, 50 cockerels and 15 foreign turkeys, said some farmers sold their birds cheaply to avoid prolonged feeding costs. He added that frozen poultry dealers also faced high electricity and preservation expenses. Mrs Oluwaseyi Fadaka, another Lokoja-based farmer, said a bag of feed now cost about N22,000, with her 40 Noiler birds consuming one regularly. She said rising feeding costs were eroding profits, forcing farmers to sell at losses or abandon the business. Fadaka said some smallholders were exploring organic feeding alternatives but needed government support through subsidised feed and affordable, quality inputs.
