item.title: Nvidia is happy to take your money whether you're using open or closed models, says Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia doesn't seem to care whether open or closed models win out as long as its hardware is powering the infrastructure. "We love closed models," CEO Jensen Huang said. "There's a solid place in the world for closed frontier models. But the world has so many good ideas … The idea that all of us would be based on general intelligence is not logical." Speaking with Lin Qiao, CEO and founder of Fireworks.ai , at the company's Forge event in San Francisco on Tuesday, Huang wasn't ready to throw Nvidia's cloud customers, which help deliver the proprietary AI of Anthropic and OpenAI, under the onrushing open model bus. But having come to the defense of open weight models in July to push back against protectionist pressure from the leadership of Anthropic and OpenAI, Huang recognizes the economic and strategic appeal of AI services that are more affordable and less locked-in. Most of the value in the world, he said, is captured in specialized intelligence, which is to say AI models trained on specific domains of knowledge. "The opportunity for artificial superintelligence is already here," he said. "By taking an open frontier model, adapting it, and providing it with your domain knowledge, your access to your specialized tools, and the proper evaluation, you should be able to create essentially a superintelligence." That aligns with Fireworks' business – offering a platform for companies to train and run models tuned to their specific needs. Coincidentally, that platform just received an infusion of 25,000 Nvidia GPUs to support its expansion in Europe . Huang's endorsement of open models also fits with Qiao's introductory remarks about the need for the AI frontier to be open. But he largely avoided echoing Qiao's focus on the cost savings allowed by working with open models. In her introductory remarks, Qiao stood on stage backlit by a slide composed of ten headlines highlighting the extraordinary cost of unchecked token spending. "Cost is out of control," she said. "Business cannot scale without borrowing a lot of money." That theme was echoed in a subsequent session helmed by Kay Zhu, co-founder and CTO of AI workspace Genspark, titled Gen-1 Slides: Frontier Quality Without Frontier Costs. Gen-1 Slides, Genspark's model for generating slide decks, was built atop MiniMax M3 and tuned to deliver results comparable to Anthropic's Opus 5 at 1/17th the cost – $0.30/M tokens compared to $5/M. Asked what might become commonplace next year but seems unlikely today, Huang said this year's breakthrough has been agent harnesses that turn AI models into agents. He added, "I would say the big breakthrough we'll talk about next year, maybe this is a little self-serving, is how Open Shell has enabled every company in the world to deploy agents safely, confidently." Given the nod to make a second prediction, Huang added, "I would say that the second big breakthrough for industry would be hardware in the loop. And hardware in the loop basically is robotic systems."
item.dc:creator: Thomas Claburn
item.content:encoded: Nvidia doesn't seem to care whether open or closed models win out as long as its hardware is powering the infrastructure. "We love closed models," CEO Jensen Huang said. "There's a solid place in the world for closed frontier models. But the world has so many good ideas … The idea that all of us would be based on general intelligence is not logical." Speaking with Lin Qiao, CEO and founder of Fireworks.ai , at the company's Forge event in San Francisco on Tuesday, Huang wasn't ready to throw Nvidia's cloud customers, which help deliver the proprietary AI of Anthropic and OpenAI, under the onrushing open model bus. But having come to the defense of open weight models in July to push back against protectionist pressure from the leadership of Anthropic and OpenAI, Huang recognizes the economic and strategic appeal of AI services that are more affordable and less locked-in. Most of the value in the world, he said, is captured in specialized intelligence, which is to say AI models trained on specific domains of knowledge. "The opportunity for artificial superintelligence is already here," he said. "By taking an open frontier model, adapting it, and providing it with your domain knowledge, your access to your specialized tools, and the proper evaluation, you should be able to create essentially a superintelligence." That aligns with Fireworks' business – offering a platform for companies to train and run models tuned to their specific needs. Coincidentally, that platform just received an infusion of 25,000 Nvidia GPUs to support its expansion in Europe . Huang's endorsement of open models also fits with Qiao's introductory remarks about the need for the AI frontier to be open. But he largely avoided echoing Qiao's focus on the cost savings allowed by working with open models. In her introductory remarks, Qiao stood on stage backlit by a slide composed of ten headlines highlighting the extraordinary cost of unchecked token spending. "Cost is out of control," she said. "Business cannot scale without borrowing a lot of money." That theme was echoed in a subsequent session helmed by Kay Zhu, co-founder and CTO of AI workspace Genspark, titled Gen-1 Slides: Frontier Quality Without Frontier Costs. Gen-1 Slides, Genspark's model for generating slide decks, was built atop MiniMax M3 and tuned to deliver results comparable to Anthropic's Opus 5 at 1/17th the cost – $0.30/M tokens compared to $5/M. Asked what might become commonplace next year but seems unlikely today, Huang said this year's breakthrough has been agent harnesses that turn AI models into agents. He added, "I would say the big breakthrough we'll talk about next year, maybe this is a little self-serving, is how Open Shell has enabled every company in the world to deploy agents safely, confidently." Given the nod to make a second prediction, Huang added, "I would say that the second big breakthrough for industry would be hardware in the loop. And hardware in the loop basically is robotic systems." Given Nvidia's evident interest and investment in robotics , that would be fortuitous. ®

item.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
item.description: null New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes. Dense stellar environments do still exist in the modern universe at the hearts of galaxies; however, these aren't conducive to the types of collisions that would birth ultra-massive stars. That is because there are already supermassive black holes at the hearts of modern galaxies, and their immense gravitational influence speeds up orbiting stars, meaning collisions that do occur are high-speed and destructive, thus failing to birth overmassive stars. "Perhaps the strangest outcome of our simulations is that stars can merge repeatedly within the cluster until they form one gigantic star with a mass equal to that of an entire cluster," team member Claire Williams, of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), said in a statement. "When a star this huge reaches the end of its life, models suggest that it may have no option but to collapse into itself and form a massive black hole." My, haven't you grown? How did supermassive black holes get so big so fast? The existence of supermassive black holes before the universe was even 1 billion years old is something that has puzzled astronomers since the JWST started spotting them in 2022. This is because black holes should need at least 1 billion years to complete the feeding and merger processes that result in a "supermassive" status of possessing millions or billions of times the mass of the sun. One suggestion put forward by scientists to explain this is that supermassive black holes don't start out from scratch. Instead, they form from black hole seeds called intermediate-mass black holes. This is considerably smaller than supermassive black holes that dominate the hearts of all modern galaxies with masses millions to billions of times the mass of our star. Intermediate-mass black holes are thought to sit between these two families of cosmic titans with masses between 100 and 100,000 times that of the sun. item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes. Dense stellar environments do still exist in the modern universe at the hearts of galaxies; however, these aren't conducive to the types of collisions that would birth ultra-massive stars. That is because there are already supermassive black holes at the hearts of modern galaxies, and their immense gravitational influence speeds up orbiting stars, meaning collisions that do occur are high-speed and destructive, thus failing to birth overmassive stars. "Perhaps the strangest outcome of our simulations is that stars can merge repeatedly within the cluster until they form one gigantic star with a mass equal to that of an entire cluster," team member Claire Williams, of the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), said in a statement. "When a star this huge reaches the end of its life, models suggest that it may have no option but to collapse into itself and form a massive black hole." My, haven't you grown? How did supermassive black holes get so big so fast? The existence of supermassive black holes before the universe was even 1 billion years old is something that has puzzled astronomers since the JWST started spotting them in 2022. This is because black holes should need at least 1 billion years to complete the feeding and merger processes that result in a "supermassive" status of possessing millions or billions of times the mass of the sun. One suggestion put forward by scientists to explain this is that supermassive black holes don't start out from scratch. Instead, they form from black hole seeds called intermediate-mass black holes. An illustration shows a massive black hole seed next to a standard stellar mass black hole (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) Normally, when a massive star collapses, it births a stellar-mass black hole possessing a mass between 10 and 100 times the mass of the sun. This is considerably smaller than supermassive black holes that dominate the hearts of all modern galaxies with masses millions to billions of times the mass of our star. Intermediate-mass black holes are thought to sit between these two families of cosmic titans with masses between 100 and 100,000 times that of the sun. The problem is, no single star should have enough mass to collapse and create an intermediate-mass black hole. But that is valid only for the conditions we see in the "modern" 13.8-billion-year-old universe in our immediate cosmic vicinity. Conditions were very different further out into the universe and further back in time. Indeed, such seeds emerged from these new simulations in environments of dense star clustering, which could solve this mystery by allowing those growth processes to get a head start. "Dense star clusters provide a natural birthplace for massive black-hole seeds in our model," Williams said. "The same environment that forms the black hole can also provide stars and gas that influence its subsequent growth." However, this could be a two-for-one deal. The JWST has also been routinely discovering astronomical bodies called Little Red Dots in the early universe. Little Red Dots are curious because they seem to have completely disappeared by the time the cosmos reached 2 billion years old. Little Red Dots the cosmic elephant in the room Little Red Dots are extremely compact objects in the early universe that get their moniker from the fact that they look like red dots. "Little Red Dots are a hot topic in astronomy. You can compare studies of people trying to understand Little Red Dots to the tale of blind people who are trying to describe an elephant by touching it, and each person describes it differently based on what part they’re touching," team member and UCLA researcher Smadar Naoz said. "Our research connects several of those perspectives together and may help us see more of the elephant." There have been many suggestions about the true nature of these objects, but one theory suggests that they possess a rapidly growing black hole at their hearts. The team's simulations suggest that Little Red Dots may be dense star clusters that are constantly being rocked by repeated stellar collisions. This results in a very large star, which eventually collapses to become an intermediate-mass black hole. But if that is the case, why were there no Little Red Dots around to celebrate the 2 billionth birthday of the universe? Just some of the "little red dot" galaxies discovered in the early universe by the JWST (Image credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Dale Kocevski (Colby College)) Less than 1 billion years after the Big Bang, the universe was devoid of well-ordered spiral galaxies, but was instead filled with dense and chaotic clusters of star birth. As these regions were rocked with frequent star collisions, the conditions were right for ultra-massive stars to form and collapse into intermediate-mass black holes. However, as the universe cooled and expanded, these sites became the building blocks of far less chaotic galaxies. Thus, if Little Red Dots are chaotic star clusters needed to form intermediate-mass black holes, progress toward an equilibrium state could explain why they suddenly disappeared from the universe. The cosmos just wasn't extreme enough to maintain Little Red Dots anymore. The team's research was published on Monday (Oct. 26) in the Astrophysical Journal.

item.title: Trump promised a 'Golden Age'. What has he delivered at home?
item.description: Donald Trump promised Americans a “Golden Age” when he returned to the White House in January 2025. Since then, his administration has slashed government spending through DOGE, ramped up mass deportations, expanded ICE operations and pursued an aggressive crackdown on DEI programmes and transgender rights. But how much has he actually achieved, and at what cost? Vedika Bahl examines Trump's domestic agenda since returning to office.

item.title: Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun
item.description: .as tension grips Ibadan community By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order. The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage. According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.” The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.” “Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“ “His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“ The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident. “Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said. However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order. The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents. Consequently, the Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, directed the deployment of additional operational assets, with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Amotekun Corps, Nigeria Security and Civil Def

item.content:encoded: .as tension grips Ibadan community By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Police Command has arrested two suspects in connection with the killing of a 26-year-old man, identified as Kehinde Asimiyu, following a fatal altercation at Olodo Garage in the Lagelu Local Government Area of Ibadan, while reinforcing security in the area to prevent a breakdown of law and order. The development came amid heightened tension in the Olodo community following the fatal stabbing of the young man, popularly known as KBlaq, by a commercial motorcyclist during a disagreement over transport fare, an incident that disrupted commercial activities and forced residents and commuters to trek considerable distances after motorcycle operators withdrew their services over fears of possible reprisal attacks. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Olayinka Ayanlade, said the command received a report of the incident on 1 November 2026, indicating that the deceased had allegedly been stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde following an altercation between the two men at Olodo Garage. According to the police, “the deceased was allegedly stabbed with a broken bottle by one Taiwo Babarinde at Olodo Garage following an altercation between both parties.” The statement added that the incident subsequently came to the attention of the deceased’s family when “an unidentified motorcycle rider arrived at their residence and informed them of the attack.” “Following receipt of the report, police operatives, accompanied by a patrol team, immediately mobilised to the scene, while the victim was rushed to Academy Hospital, Texaco, Iwo Road, Ibadan, where he was confirmed dead by the doctor on duty.“ “His remains were subsequently deposited at Adejare Embalming Centre for preservation, while photographs were taken as part of the preliminary investigative procedures.“ The police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding the killing had led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as Taiwo Babarinde, suspected to have inflicted the fatal injury on the deceased, and Ishola Semiu, suspected of involvement in the incident. “Both suspects are currently in Police custody, while the case has been transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID), Iyaganku, Ibadan, for comprehensive investigation,” the statement said. However, the police intervention following the killing also witnessed a fresh security challenge, as unrest reportedly erupted at the Olodo Police Outpost, nearly resulting in a breakdown of law and order. The situation was further compounded by subsequent reports of threats from hoodlums, prompting the immediate reinforcement of security across the area to prevent further disturbances and protect residents. Consequently, the Commissioner of Police, CP Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, directed the deployment of additional operational assets, with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Amotekun Corps, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other local law enforcement components joining the security operation. The command said the coordinated deployment had helped restore normalcy, adding that there was now a sustained security presence in the area “to forestall further disturbances and protect residents.” In a further move to address the underlying tensions, the Commissioner of Police directed the Area Commander, Moniya, to engage relevant community stakeholders towards addressing the situation and preventing a recurrence. Acting on the directive, the Area Commander earlier on Tuesday held a strategic meeting with representatives of the Local Council Development Area (LCDA), leaders of tricycle and motorcycle operators, as well as youth leaders. The engagement, according to the police, “focused on identifying practical solutions, strengthening communication with security agencies and promoting peaceful coexistence among residents and other stakeholders.” Reassuring residents of the command’s commitment to their safety, the police said: “The Command reassures residents of Olodo and its environs that adequate security measures remain in place to safeguard lives and property.” The command also issued a stern warning to those seeking to exploit the situation to foment trouble, incite violence or destabilise the area. “It also issues a stern warning to individuals or groups seeking to foment trouble, incite violence or exploit the situation to destabilise the area that such conduct will not be tolerated,” the statement added. It further declared that: “The Command will decisively deal with anyone whose actions threaten public peace or undermine the security gains recorded across Oyo State.” The Commissioner of Police also appealed to residents to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating the crisis. He urged them to “remain calm, shun violence and embrace dialogue as a means of resolving disagreements.” He further encouraged community members to cooperate with security agencies by providing credible and timely information, while reiterating the command’s determination to sustain the prevailing peace and ensure the safety and security of all residents. The post Olodo murder: Police arrest two suspects, deploy Army, Amotekun appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Voting in space: NASA astronauts cast ballots from International Space Station
item.description: null The three Americans currently living off Earth just made sure their electoral voices were heard. Anil Menon told us today (Nov. 3) that he and fellow NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins voted in the U.S. midterm elections from the International Space Station (ISS). "Yes, you can even vote from space! All three U.S. crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials," Menon wrote in an X post this morning . Yes, you can even vote from space! All three US crew members had the privilege of voting from space station. We filled out an electronic ballot and sent it securely to the election officials. https://t.co/hJCExQ2nKr November 3, 2026 That post included a 29-second video, in which Menon — wearing, like many of us today, an "I voted" sticker — shows us his "voting booth." It's actually his room on the ISS, Menon explained. "Inside of it is my computer, where I was able to fill out an electronic form and send it to Harris County so I could vote today," he said. Most NASA astronauts register to vote in Texas' Harris County; it's home to Johnson Space Center in Houston, the agency's human spaceflight hub. Americans have been able to vote from space since 1997, when Texas passed a law allowing this to happen. The first person to take advantage of the legislation was NASA astronaut David Wolf, who cast his ballot from Russia's Mir space station that same year. (The ISS didn't welcome its first crew until November 2000.) "Just like any other American away from home, astronauts may fill out a Federal Post Card Application to request an absentee ballot," NASA officials wrote in an astronaut-voting explainer . The process is somewhat involved, however. "After an astronaut fills out an electronic ballot aboard the orbiting laboratory, the document flows through NASA's Tracking and Data Relay Satellite System to a ground antenna at the agency's White Sands Test Facility in Las Cruces, New Mexico," they added. "From New Mexico, NASA transfers the ballot to the Mission Control Center at NASA Johnson and then on to the county clerk responsible for casting the ballot. To preserve the vote's integrity, the ballot is encrypted and accessible only by the astronaut and the clerk." NASA's Near Space Network enables astronauts on the International Space Station to communicate with Earth and electronically deliver ballots from space. (Image credit: NASA) Delaney and Watkins launched to the ISS on Oct. 1 on SpaceX's Crew-13 mission . Menon has been there since mid-July, arriving aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft . The trio currently share the orbiting lab with four other people — Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk and cosmonauts Anna Kikina, Pyotr Dubrov and Sergey Teteryatnikov. Kutryk and Teteryatnikov are members of Crew-13, whereas Dubrov and Kikina shared the Soyuz with Menon.

item.title: Ogun govt, Ijebu Chiefs clash over Awujale Council as succession crisis deepens
item.description: …State reconstitutes AIAC, insists Adele Oba Awujale group lacks legal backing By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta A fresh controversy has erupted over the administration of Ijebuland following the decision of the Ogun State government to reconstitute the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC), barely a day after traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode announced the dissolution of the council and its replacement with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The development has exposed a disagreement between the state government and some traditional authorities over the appropriate legal and customary structure for administering Ijebuland pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale. While the government insists that the AIAC remains the only legally recognised administrative body authorised to oversee the affairs of Ijebuland during the interregnum, the traditional chiefs maintain that the Adele Oba Awujale in Council is rooted in the customs and established traditional practices of the Ijebu people. In a statement issued on Tuesday by the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Hon. Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities. The government described the AIAC, established in August 2025, as the only legally recognised administrative structure empowered to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland until a new Awujale is appointed and crowned. It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council. Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State. According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool. The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976. To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others. It said the judgment affirmed the legality, validity and authority of the AIAC as the administrative body established by the government to oversee the affairs of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coro

Ganiyu Hamzat, the state government said the withdrawal of some members of the AIAC did not invalidate the council or confer legal authority on another body to take over its responsibilities. It specifically clarified that Chief Chris Okunowo and Alhaji Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, had publicly dissociated themselves from the reported mass withdrawal from the council. Dismissing the emergence of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, the government maintained that the body had no legal or customary recognition under the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration or the existing chieftaincy laws of Ogun State. According to Hamzat, neither the Awujale Chieftaincy Declaration nor the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law 2021 makes provision for an Adele Oba Awujale group or assigns it any recognised responsibility in the administration of the vacant Awujale stool. The government also faulted the reliance on the Chiefs Law of 1957 by some former members to justify the emergence of the new body, arguing that the legislation was enacted before Nigeria’s independence and no longer applied to Ogun State, which had operated under its own laws since its creation in 1976. To support its position, the state government cited a consent judgment delivered by the Ogun State High Court in suit number HCJ/180/2025, involving Rasheed Adeoye Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, against the Executive Council of Ogun State and 16 others. It said the judgment affirmed the legality, validity and authority of the AIAC as the administrative body established by the government to oversee the affairs of Ijebu-Ode pending the appointment and coronation of a new Awujale. The government noted that all members of the council were parties to the suit and had consented to the judgment. It further stated that the court had affirmed that where there was a conflict between the administrative responsibilities of the AIAC and the traditional functions of the Olisa, the authority of the administrative body would take precedence. The statement added that the judgment had not been appealed and remained binding on the parties. Although acknowledging the right of individual members to withdraw from the council, the government warned that such a decision could not confer legal authority on another group to assume the functions of the AIAC. It consequently cautioned members of the public against conducting official transactions or administrative dealings with individuals who had withdrawn from the council in their purported capacity as members of an alternative administrative body. The government also urged the former members to refrain from actions capable of violating the law or threatening peace and stability in Ijebuland. Consequently, it announced the reconstitution of the AIAC to ensure continuity in the administration of the ancient town. The reconstituted council comprises Chief Rasheed Adesanya, the Olisa of Ijebu-Ode, as Chairman; Chief Chris Okunowo, Bobasuwa, as Secretary; Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso; Chief Stephen O. Bakare, Babalaje; and Chief Alade Shote, Otun Balogun, as members. The government said the council would continue to discharge its legally recognised administrative and traditional responsibilities until a new Awujale was appointed and crowned. ……..Chiefs insist on traditional authority However, the government’s position came against the backdrop of a resolution adopted on Monday by traditional chiefs in Ijebu-Ode to dissolve the AIAC and replace it with the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The resolution was reached at a meeting involving the Ilamuren, Pampa, the Odi and other traditional chiefs of Ijebu-Ode, where the leaders reportedly agreed that members of the existing AIAC should step down from their positions and assume membership of the newly constituted body. The state government had established the AIAC in August 2025, about a month after the death of the 91-year-old Awujale, Oba Sikiru Adetona, in July 2025, to manage the administrative and traditional affairs of Ijebuland during the transition period. The initial administrative arrangement was chaired by Chief Folorunso Kuku, the Ogbeni Oja of Ijebuland and co-founder of EKO Hospital, Lagos, who is also designated as one of the Ilamuren. But in a resolution signed by the Chairman of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council, Olo’rgun Dr Sonny Kuku, the traditional chiefs said their decision to replace the AIAC was informed by their interpretation of the existing traditional and statutory frameworks governing the Awujale chieftaincy institution. They argued that the Ogun State Chiefs Law 2021 did not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council or prescribe a general procedure for appointing a regent during an interregnum. The chiefs, however, maintained that the Chiefs Law and the 1957 Declaration provided a framework for recognising customary arrangements, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council. The resolution stated: “Upon consideration of the applicable traditional and statutory framework, it was observed that the Ogun State Chiefs Law of 2021 does not expressly establish an Awujale Regency Council, nor does it prescribe a general procedure for the appointment of a Regent.” It added: “It was further noted that the Chiefs Law and Declaration of 1957 provide an existing framework within which customary declarations are made and recognised, including the traditional institution of the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.” Explaining the decision to replace the AIAC, the chiefs said: “In view of the foregoing, a motion was moved and unanimously adopted that all members of the Awujale Interregnum Administrative Council (AIAC) should formally step down from their existing positions and transition into the Adele Oba Awujale in Council.” They further declared that the new body would assume responsibility for the administration of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum. “Consequently, the Adele Oba Awujale in Council shall henceforth assume responsibility for the administration of the affairs of Ijebu-Ode during the interregnum and exercise, on an interim basis, such administrative powers and functions as may appropriately be required in the absence of the Awujale, subject to applicable laws and established customs and traditions,” the resolution stated. The 14-member Adele Oba Awujale in Council comprises Dr Sonny Kuku, who holds the Ogbeni Oja title; Chief Rasheed Adesanya, Olisa; Chief O.B. Okuboyejo, Obasewa; Chief Chris Funmilola Okunowo, Bobasuwa; and Chief Prof. Jide Ajayi, Jagun Aso. Other members are Chief Oluwaranti Lekan Osif

item.title: Ukraine’s drone strikes spur hasty Russian plans for underground data centers
item.description: Russian tech companies are scrambling to harden and hide their data centers underground after Ukrainian drone strikes damaged facilities housing AI supercomputers and disrupted cloud services for millions of Russian users. Meanwhile, the Kremlin is requiring data center owners to reserve computing capacity for emergency state needs and has even authorized possible use of foreign data centers. These consequences of Russia's war against Ukraine come as the Russian military has bombarded Ukrainian cities with drones and missiles nearly night and day in recent months, along with specifically targeting Ukrainian data centers since late September. But Ukraine has retaliated with its own drone strikes on military and infrastructure targets across Russia, degrading or knocking out data centers operated by Russian tech giant Yandex , the state-owned bank Sberbank, social media site VKontakte, and the Russian Ministry of Finance. Now, state-owned telecommunications company Rostelcom has raised the possibility of moving some Russian data centers underground in talks with the nickel and palladium mining company Norilsk, according to Russian newspaper Vedomosti . The industry publication Data Center Dynamics also pointed to a recent proposal by a Russian regional governor to build data centers within open-pit coal mines while planting green public parks above as camouflage. Read full article Comments

item.title: Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards
item.description: The Federal Government has paid cash rewards to players, coaches and officials of the Super Falcons following their victory at the 2025 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), completing the reward package promised by President Bola Tinubu. The National Sports Commission (NSC) disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Head of Press and Public Relations, Zira Zakka Nagga. According to the commission, each player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while each coach and official received the equivalent of $50,000. The team had earlier received the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON) and three-bedroom apartments. The Chairman of the NSC, Shehu Dikko, thanked Tinubu for fulfilling his pledge, saying the President had directed that all aspects of the reward package be delivered within a reasonable time. “The Super Falcons made Nigeria proud, and Mr President has honoured his commitment to them in full. This means a great deal to the team and to Nigerian sports,” Dikko said. He said the President’s action marked a departure from previous experiences in which some Nigerian athletes waited years to receive promised rewards. “Some of our sports heroes endured years of waiting for promises to be fulfilled. President Tinubu has shown that things can be done differently,” he said. Dikko added that the fulfilment of the pledge would encourage athletes to represent the country with confidence that their efforts would be recognised. He also said the gesture would inspire young Nigerians, particularly girls aspiring to pursue careers in sports. The NSC chairman recalled that Nigeria’s senior women’s basketball team, D’Tigress, received similar cash rewards in September 2026 after winning their fifth consecutive FIBA Women’s AfroBasket title in 2025. Each D’Tigress player received the naira equivalent of $100,000, while officials received $50,000 each. The team had also received three-bedroom apartments and national honours. Dikko also cited the completion of rewards for the Super Eagles following their silver-medal finish at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations, held in Côte d’Ivoire in 2024. He thanked the Ministers of Finance, Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, and Housing and Urban Development for their roles in completing the reward package. “Delivering these rewards required close cooperation across government. We appreciate the Honourable Ministers and their teams for working with the Commission to complete the necessary processes,” he said. The commission congratulated the Super Falcons’ players, coaches and officials on their achievement, urging Nigerian athletes preparing for future competitions to draw encouragement from the fulfilment of the President’s promises. It quoted Tinubu as saying: “My promise to every Nigerian athlete is: make Nigeria proud, and come back to a grateful nation.” The post Tinubu fulfils pledge as Super Falcons receive $100,000 cash rewards appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Magic: The Gathering Is Reprinting a Powerful $30 Sword With Perfect Pixel Art
item.description: Magic: The Gathering is reaching into its inventory of powerful artifacts to reprint a sword worth nearly $30, complete with gloriously nostalgic video game artwork. Sword of Truth and Justice , a popular Equipment first released in 2019, is returning in a new Secret Lair collection that draws inspiration from the blocky, polygonal graphics of the Nintendo 64 and original PlayStation era.

item.title: Arteta backs Saliba’s readiness to return for Arsenal at Slavia Prague
item.description: Defender travelled with squad after long injury absence ‘I have clips’: Arteta hits back after Liverpool complaints Mikel Arteta is confident that William Saliba is ready to make his first appearance of the season for Arsenal after he played 45 minutes of a match behind closed doors last week. The France defender started training on his own last month after the back injury he sustained at the World Cup but has since resumed full training and on Tuesday travelled with Arsenal’s squad to face Slavia Prague. It remains to be seen whether Saliba will feature in the Czech capital given such a lengthy absence, although Arteta insisted that he has no doubts the 25-year-old is primed to return. item.title: Atiku Alleges Plot To Disrupt ADC Campaign In Sokoto, Vows Resistance
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of working to frustrate the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in the state, alleging that protesters were being mobilised to disrupt the party’s planned rally. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Among his proposals is a targeted production subsidy linked to fuel refined in Nigeria. He said the measure would ease the burden on consumers while supporting domestic industry. The ADC candidate further alleged that the APC had turned to intimidation following what he called a disappointing turnout at its most recent rally in Kaduna. “The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence,” he said. With the 2027 elections approaching, Atiku described the contest as a critical test of the country’s democracy, framing it as a choice between the Tinubu administration, which he accused of disregarding Nigerians’ hardship, and those seeking a change in direction. He maintained that the alleged obstacles would not stop the ADC from campaigning and said he would personally attend the Sokoto rally on Wednesday. “Our campaign will proceed, and I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state,” he said. He asked residents to avoid violence and urged security agencies to ensure the safety of people going about their daily activities as well as those attending the rally. Atiku also cautioned that any security officer found to have participated in efforts to restrict political activity would face accountability under the law. item.title: Google says there’s no way to use Search without using artificial intelligence
item.description: In announcement geared to schools, tech giant shows how entwined AI is with the world’s most popular website Google just acknowledged that you can’t use Google Search without using artificial intelligence . The search giant announced a slate of new AI products for classrooms and schools on Tuesday as well as more ways for teachers and schools to limit or restrict use of those AI tools. The company said the schools should have control over whether students use AI in the classroom. There’s one catch, though: if a school or teacher blocks the use of Google’s AI features, students won’t be able to use Google Search. Continue reading...

item.title: The Pixel Buds Pro 2 have returned to their lowest price to date
item.description: Android owners looking for an earbud upgrade are in luck. The Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 are back down to $169 at Amazon , Best Buy , and the Google Store , matching the lowest price we’ve seen. Google’s site claims the deal will last until 11:59PM PT on November 8th, and other retailers will likely follow suit. Some colors are already sold out, however, so it’s worth checking multiple retailers if you don’t see your preferred option. Google Pixel Buds Pro 2 Where to Buy: $229 $169 at Amazon $229 $169 at Google Store $229 $169 at Best Buy The Pro 2 are great for Android owners and work particularly well with Pixel phones, which receive some extra tricks, including tighter Gemini integration. We praised the wireless earbuds for their improved design, which cut both weight and size while improving the comfort and fit. They have more powerful noise cancellation and a better transparency mode, though they still don’t quite match up to some of the best in the industry, like the latest Bose Ultra Earbuds . The default tuning leans towards clarity and crisp detail, rather than boosted bass, with both presets and a five-band EQ to adjust them to your liking. Read our full Pixel Buds Pro 2 review . Other deals to consider Nintendo Switch owners can pick up Borderlands: Game of the Year Edition from the Nintendo Store for just $5.99, a steep discount from the usual price of $29.99. The updated version of the first game in Gearbox’s storied looter-shooter series features “bazillions” of guns, visual upgrades, and all four of the DLC packs. The deal runs until 11:59PM PT on November 6th. The refurbished Fellow Aiden is on sale at Fellow’s online storefront for $299.95, a $100 discount. The coffee maker brews anywhere from a single cup to a full carafe of pour-over-quality coffee, with scheduling available both on the machine and via the Aiden app. Refurb units have been thoroughly tested and come with a one-year warranty, too, just in case there are any issues. Prime Members can score a 26 percent discount on ESR’s Cyclone Magnetic Charging Pad at Amazon, lowering the price of the silver and black units to $36.99 ($13 off). The wireless charger supports up to 25 watts, with a built-in fan to keep both the charger and your device cool. The integrated stand also lets you use the charger while you catch up on YouTube, and the 5.9-foot cable means you aren’t glued to an outlet.

item.title: Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State. The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lt. Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lokoja. Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements. He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat. “The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said. A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles. Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups. He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State. The post Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation appeared first on Vanguard News .
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles and thousands of rounds of ammunition during a follow-up operation in Kogi State. The operation took place on Tuesday in Edimogbo Forest, Igalamela-Odolu Local Government Area, as troops continued efforts to track fleeing suspects following a raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the same forest on Monday. The Acting Assistant Director, Army Public Relations, 12 Composite Brigade, Lt. Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday in Lokoja. Abdullahi said troops sustained their operations in the forest to locate fleeing suspects, clear remaining hideouts and restrict the movement of criminal elements. He said the troops made contact with the suspects during the follow-up operation and engaged them, forcing them to retreat. “The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of two kidnappers, while others fled into the surrounding forest,” he said. A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, seven magazines, 438 rounds of 7.62mm x 54 ammunition and 4,725 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition. Other items recovered included two bandoliers, two mobile phones and a power bank. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that troops had dismantled a suspected kidnappers’ camp in the forest during Monday’s operation, recovering about 1,000 rounds of ammunition and six motorcycles. Abdullahi said Tuesday’s operation had consolidated the gains of the earlier raid, adding that troops remained committed to sustaining pressure on criminal groups. He said the brigade would continue operations to protect lives and property and support efforts to restore lasting peace across Kogi State. The post Army neutralises 2 kidnappers in Kogi follow-up operation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
item.description: Apple will now let Siri AI perform actions across third-party apps. As part of the iOS 27.3 update rolling out on Tuesday, Apple announced developers can now integrate Siri AI's new features in "all apps," allowing the voice assistant to draw on a user's personal context, process natural language prompts, and use on-screen awareness to complete requests. The update, which is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview, also adds a new "app skills" feature that third-party developers can create to combine several tasks into a single action. item.title: Toluwanisings: Oyo Police summon wife, father, friends as parties sign peace deal
item.description: The Oyo State Police Command has brokered peace between the family and associates of late Nigerian singer Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, following disagreements over his burial arrangements. The intervention comes amid allegations of conspiracy, defamation of character and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace, which reportedly generated public exchanges between parties on social media and other communication platforms. In a statement on Tuesday, the Command said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received information about the dispute on October 28, 2026, and subsequently directed the parties to appear at the Command Headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention. The police said the meeting, which was held on November 3, resulted in the parties signing a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. Those involved included the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as his personal assistant and other representatives. According to the statement, the parties agreed to maintain peace, exhibit good behaviour and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions surrounding the singer’s death and burial arrangements. The statement reads, “Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. “Under the terms of the undertaking, all parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace, and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions capable of inflaming tensions or aggravating the existing disagreement surrounding the unfortunate demise of the singer and related issues. “Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives. They equally agreed not to grant interviews, provide access or facilitate engagements with individuals or media platforms for the purpose of further disseminating such narratives. In addition, each party undertook to direct their respective proxies and associates to desist from making, sponsoring, amplifying or circulating publications capable of reigniting the disagreement or undermining the peace agreement. “In reinforcing the terms of the undertaking

The intervention comes amid allegations of conspiracy, defamation of character and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace, which reportedly generated public exchanges between parties on social media and other communication platforms. In a statement on Tuesday, the Command said the Commissioner of Police, Abimbola Ayodeji Olugbenga, received information about the dispute on October 28, 2026, and subsequently directed the parties to appear at the Command Headquarters in Eleyele, Ibadan, for an intervention. The police said the meeting, which was held on November 3, resulted in the parties signing a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. Those involved included the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as his personal assistant and other representatives. According to the statement, the parties agreed to maintain peace, exhibit good behaviour and refrain from actions capable of escalating tensions surrounding the singer’s death and burial arrangements. The statement reads, “Consequently, at the conclusion of the engagement held today, 3rd November 2026, all parties, comprising the deceased’s wife, Mrs Olayemi Elizabeth Damilola; his father, Mr Muniru Olayemi; his friends and associates, including Oyindamola Esther, Babadunni Gbolabo and Comrade Lawal Ademola Rafiu, as well as the deceased’s personal assistant and other representatives, entered into and signed a peace undertaking before the Commissioner of Police. “Under the terms of the undertaking, all parties agreed to maintain peace and be of good behaviour, refrain from any act capable of causing a breach of the peace, and discontinue public exchanges, interviews and discussions capable of inflaming tensions or aggravating the existing disagreement surrounding the unfortunate demise of the singer and related issues. “Furthermore, the parties expressly undertook to discontinue the dissemination of information, narratives, allegations and publications relating to the matter through social media platforms, print media, radio, blogs and other communication channels, including publications made through their respective proxies, agents, associates and representatives. They equally agreed not to grant interviews, provide access or facilitate engagements with individuals or media platforms for the purpose of further disseminating such narratives. In addition, each party undertook to direct their respective proxies and associates to desist from making, sponsoring, amplifying or circulating publications capable of reigniting the disagreement or undermining the peace agreement. “In reinforcing the terms of the undertaking, the Commissioner of Police warned that the agreement must be respected by all parties and extended to their proxies, agents, associates and representatives. He cautioned that no individual should take advantage of the unfortunate circumstances surrounding the singer’s demise to instigate hostility, promote unsubstantiated allegations or engage in conduct capable of disrupting public peace. Any person whose actions constitute an offence under applicable laws will be arrested and prosecuted accordingly.” The Command also appealed to members of the public, bloggers and media practitioners to exercise restraint and avoid amplifying unverified information capable of reigniting tensions. It urged all concerned to respect the commitments made during the peace meeting, adding that any conduct independently amounting to a criminal offence would be addressed in accordance with the law. item.title: Phil Foden sets sights on England recall and says he has had no contact with Tuchel
item.description: Foden: ‘You have to keep putting on performances’ Enzo Maresca: ‘We cannot rely on Erling for every game’ Phil Foden is aiming for an England recall after the Manchester City attacker was left out of the squad for last summer’s World Cup and the Nations League games this season by Thomas Tuchel. While the next round of England games in the competition – the squad for which will be named on Friday – may come too soon for a recall, Foden wants to force his way back into Tuchel’s plans. The 26-year-old said: “Hopefully, one day the call-up might come back. It’s one of those things [being dropped]. Football is full of ups and downs. You have to try your best, keep putting on performances.” Continue reading...

item.title: British fintech Revolut slashes AI coding costs 10x by cutting out Claude and going self-hosted
item.description: Revolut says that in less than a year it's managed to slash its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude. Speaking at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month, David Abitbol, ops and infrastructure lead at the British fintech, described how it saw a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time following its rollout of AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. Revolut initially adopted GLM-5.1 before moving to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. Prior to its switch to GLM, Revolut had been experimenting with AI, deploying Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said. Because of this, engineers only had access to a limited number of tokens, so the company began investigating self-hosting its own models. At $0.30 per million input/output tokens, self hosting GLM 5.1 cost about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. And, as it turned out, when tokens are cheap, you stop worrying about how many they use or what they use them for. While Revolut did see improvements to coding speed, Abitbol noted the biggest bottleneck wasn't actually the code. Instead, he says the biggest gains came from letting the AI models deal with things like debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task." Developed by Chinese open weights model dev Z.ai, GLM 5.1 isn't exactly a small model. At roughly 754 billion total parameters (40 billion activated for each token generated), the model requires roughly 380 GB of GPU memory just to hold the weights and another 6-26 GB per user to maintain context depending on precision. To serve GLM-5.3 at scale, Revolut deployed 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, equivalent in GPU count to seven eight-GPU DGX B200 systems. But as Abitbol noted, the greatest performance gains didn't come from adding GPUs, but rather tuning the model's hyperparameters along with switching to NVFP4 quantization, implementing disaggregated prefill and decode, and tuning context lengths. One key takeaway was that supporting a one-million-token context window doesn't necessarily make such a large window useful or efficient. "Long context is a scam. You really need to be mindful of that," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need." With these optimizations, Abitbol says that the company was able to achieve sub 3-second time to first token on context windows of around 256,000 tokens, and generation speeds of around 200 tokens a second, both of which he note
item.dc:creator: Tobias Mann
item.content:encoded: Revolut says that in less than a year it's managed to slash its AI coding inference costs by roughly 90 percent by making self-hosted models its default instead of relying primarily on commercial services like Claude. Speaking at the AI Engineer conference in New York last month, David Abitbol, ops and infrastructure lead at the British fintech, described how it saw a 60 percent improvement in coding time and a 70 percent improvement in lead time following its rollout of AI coding tools to roughly 2,000 engineers. Revolut initially adopted GLM-5.1 before moving to GLM-5.3, which it now serves using 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. Prior to its switch to GLM, Revolut had been experimenting with AI, deploying Gemini in early 2025 and Claude Code in early 2026. "We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI. We were seeing engineers spend $1,000 a month, $10,000 a month with not so much ROI, and so when we launched it we launched it with strict budget limits," Abitbol said. Because of this, engineers only had access to a limited number of tokens, so the company began investigating self-hosting its own models. At $0.30 per million input/output tokens, self hosting GLM 5.1 cost about a tenth of using OpenAI's Codex or Anthropic's Claude Code. And, as it turned out, when tokens are cheap, you stop worrying about how many they use or what they use them for. While Revolut did see improvements to coding speed, Abitbol noted the biggest bottleneck wasn't actually the code. Instead, he says the biggest gains came from letting the AI models deal with things like debugging and Jira and Confluence tickets. "When you have unlimited tokens, you're free to do that," he said. "You no longer have to save your tokens for the end of the quarter or the most difficult task." Developed by Chinese open weights model dev Z.ai, GLM 5.1 isn't exactly a small model. At roughly 754 billion total parameters (40 billion activated for each token generated), the model requires roughly 380 GB of GPU memory just to hold the weights and another 6-26 GB per user to maintain context depending on precision. To serve GLM-5.3 at scale, Revolut deployed 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs, equivalent in GPU count to seven eight-GPU DGX B200 systems. But as Abitbol noted, the greatest performance gains didn't come from adding GPUs, but rather tuning the model's hyperparameters along with switching to NVFP4 quantization, implementing disaggregated prefill and decode, and tuning context lengths. One key takeaway was that supporting a one-million-token context window doesn't necessarily make such a large window useful or efficient. "Long context is a scam. You really need to be mindful of that," Abitbol said. "Even though you can serve one million tokens, 256 [thousand] is really what you need." With these optimizations, Abitbol says that the company was able to achieve sub 3-second time to first token on context windows of around 256,000 tokens, and generation speeds of around 200 tokens a second, both of which he notes are the sweet spot for the company's software engineers. "What you want to aim for is a sub-3 second time to first token. This is empirical evidence. As soon as you exceed 5 seconds, my Slack inbox starts to blow up," Abitbol said. "In terms of throughput, it doesn't really matter as much. We serve, in terms of interactivity, 200 tokens per second. People are fine [with that]. You don't need to go higher. The way people work has changed. We no longer look at the stream of thinking tokens. People run tasks in parallel and check in when the task is done." And if throughput is a concern, he notes engineers who sign in after 5 pm are getting closer to 800 tokens a second. However, it's worth noting that GLM hasn't replaced GPT or Claude entirely. The Chinese model is text only, so it isn't ideal for things like UI work. So instead, Revolut used a model router to direct vision queries to models like Gemini or GPT Luna while keeping code generation running on GLM. "Open source is now a priority at Revolut, and our economics are favorable. The billing is flat, we don't have any bill shock at the end of the month, and the frontier is the exception," Abitbol said. Having said that, Abitbol acknowledges that Chinese open weights models may be a concern for privacy and security reasons, but emphasizes that the major concern there is accessing them via APIs running out of China. When run on-prem or on regional cloud resources, there's really nothing to worry about. ®

item.title: 'OGame' developers explain how the browser-based sci-fi game has lasted 24 years ahead of the huge Orion update
item.description: If you were on the Internet in the early 2000s looking for free browser games to play, OGame was a blooming sci-fi strategy sensation that couldn't be ignored. With online servers providing the structure for a living and evolving universe where players fought, traded, and created empires from scratch, its limited visual presentation was no issue. Times have changed, but GameForge hasn't gone anywhere. OGame has been ported to mobile devices, and content updates have kept it alive and fresh for much longer than a plethora of installable MMO games. With the Orion update , which will hit the newly launched universes (servers) on November 6, OGame is introducing conflicts against non-player-character (NPC) enemies, wave-based battles, co-op missions, and completely new systems that can also be disrupted by other players. The game's endurance and such a major reinvention are stunning achievements, so we asked GameForge's Martin Liedtke (Director, Products of Browser Games) and Enrico Mareth (Senior Project Manager for OGame PC and Mobile) about the many challenges of working on OGame alongside the community for so long, what Orion is bringing to the table, and what's next for this worldwide phenomenon. Some quotes have been editorialized and lightly trimmed for better flow. (Image credit: Gameforge) "OGame has an enduring core: You build an interstellar empire, and your decisions matter... Keeping it fresh means adding meaningful choices to that foundation," said Liedtke. "Orion adds missions against automated opponents (PvE) alongside missions open to other players (PvP)... It supports different appetites for risk." The GameForge veteran noted, however, that it's the community that "supplies another kind of freshness" after the studio releases the new content. "We develop the systems; players create much of the history." Part of this approach is keeping tabs on how very different kinds of players approach what's available. "Some commanders concentrate on their economy; others enjoy expeditions or carefully coordinated fleet operations... Orion follows that approach; more experienced players can dig into fleet composition, progression, and cooperation. The aim is to offer worthwhile choices." Liedtke also noted that "OGame's PvP has become a sophisticated contest of information and coordination" over time. Some players like to scout targets and organize combined attacks when enemy fleets are vulnerable. Those battles resolve automatically, but it's the planning that "can be remarkably intricate," especially after so many years of updates. The PvE in Orion doesn't sacrifice any of those intricacies or density. In fact, it's adding a "more structured layer" that gives players clear objectives. In most cases, they'll have to cooperate to obtain better rewards. "There is a strong case for introducing that kind of cooperative PvE earlier.
